Owned object

one versioned inbound event and its private draft disposition

Healthy / done condition

The event has exactly one reconstructable draft outcome or a visible terminal failure, cancellation, or abstention; no external side effect occurred.

Progressive tutorial

From first run to safe operation.

01

Try it

Run the deterministic pilot once on synthetic events and inspect private drafts.

  • install the locked environment with uv sync --frozen
  • run the supplied synthetic fixture through the local adapter
  • confirm outputs remain drafts with exact evidence and no side effects

Exit: The sample run finishes with deterministic drafts and no external action.

02

Run it repeatedly

Prove replay, ordering, recovery, and evaluation behavior are repeatable.

  • run all repository and tutorial tests
  • run the frozen evaluation and inspect raw numerators and denominators
  • exercise serial, concurrent, reordered, failed, cancelled, and recovered cases

Exit: All frozen tests and zero-failure invariants pass repeatedly.

03

Operate it safely

Understand the controls required before adapting the playbook to live systems.

  • review permissions, approvals, threat model, failure matrix, and runbook
  • keep the adapter no-write until a separately reviewed T2 contract exists
  • retest after every permission, policy, runtime, dependency, model, adapter, or incident change
  • use the owner-controlled kill switch and evidence-bound reconciliation procedure

Exit: Operators can identify authorization, approval, monitoring, recovery, escalation, and stop boundaries without inferring them from prompt text.

Verification evidence

How you know.

  • current-policy authorization decision
  • exact source version and UTF-8 byte evidence spans
  • durable fenced ledger state
  • redacted transition, plan, retry, and outcome telemetry
  • frozen evaluation metrics and adversarial regression results

Stop · approve · escalate

Where autonomy ends.

  • stop on authorization, validation, telemetry, deadline, conflict, or kill-switch failure
  • abstain on unsupported or contradictory evidence
  • route sensitive matches to the named owner
  • leave every final disposition to Anushrut Gupta outside this no-write adapter

Operational contract

What this playbook guarantees—and does not.

Success criteria

  • Frozen ordinary cases route according to deterministic policy.
  • Unsupported and contradictory cases abstain.
  • Sensitive cases escalate to security and remain owned by Anushrut Gupta.
  • Serial, concurrent, reordered, and recovered replay yield one semantic outcome.
  • Denied, failed, cancelled, retried, succeeded, and recovered histories are reconstructable.

Unacceptable outcomes

  • Source text changes permissions, policy, recipients, tools, approval, or impact.
  • Unauthorized or revoked records reveal content or produce a suggestion.
  • Same event identity with changed content produces a second semantic outcome.
  • Stale, malformed, conflicting, or unsupported input is silently treated as ordinary.
  • Work continues after deadline or kill-switch activation.
  • A suggestion is sent, committed, or finalized automatically.

Non-goals

  • Send a response or alert.
  • Close, assign, update, create, or publish an external record.
  • Make a high-stakes or final disposition.
  • Claim production routing accuracy or live-source compatibility.

Limitations

  • No live source, credential, model, network, recurring trigger, or external destination is included.
  • SQLite state is durable across local adapter processes and restarts sharing one filesystem, but is not a multi-host or distributed ledger.
  • Keyword routing is illustrative and not a production classifier.
  • Timeout enforcement is cooperative at declared step fences; this no-I/O deterministic adapter has no blocking external dependency to preempt.
  • Awaiting-approval and partial-side-effect paths are present in the neutral state vocabulary but unreachable in this T1 no-write adapter.
